rows.jp: 提案した当人が驚きやがった。
rows.en: The one who’d suggested it had the nerve to act surprised.

ghs.en: Even the very person who suggested it was surprised.

rows.jp: 「冬子を餓えさせるにはいかないだろう？」
rows.en: “I can’t let Touko starve, can I?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I can't just starve you, Touko, can I?"

rows.jp: 「食の誘惑に取り憑かれたハラヘリハラキリ餓狼を世に解きはなつことになるしな」
rows.en: “Otherwise I’d be turning a food-crazed Hangry-Harakiri Hunger-Wolf loose on the world.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "We can't get to the point where the Hankerin' Harakiri Hungry Wolf becomes possessed by the allure of food and is unleashed on the world."

rows.jp: 「あ、あの、すぐ着替えとか持ってくるからっ」
rows.en: “I-I’ll go get a change of clothes and everything right now!”

ghs.en: Touko: "Ah, uhm, I'm just going to bring back a change of clothes!"

ghs.assessment: The source comically uses the English loan 'waits' and then glosses it as 待て. The translation replaces that English with Japanese 'Matte,' reversing the language joke.
ghs.remedy: Use 'WAIT! (Wait!)' or another rendering that preserves the English-loan-plus-gloss structure.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Matte! (Wait!)"

rows.jp: 冬子は地面にキスした。

ghs.en: Touko implemented a kiss with the ground.
ghs.assessment: The source says Tōko kissed the ground. 'Implemented a kiss with the ground' is bureaucratic, unidiomatic English and obscures the physical gag.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Tōko kissed the ground.'

highlights.text: Touko implemented a kiss with the ground.

ghs.en: Good thing that we're on the lawn.
Taichi: "Good thing that we're on the lawn."
I directly contacted my true intentions.
ghs.assessment: 本音で接した means the narrator dealt with her honestly or spoke from the heart. 'Contacted my true intentions' turns sincerity into an object contacted and is not grammatical English.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I spoke from the heart.'

highlights.text: I directly contacted my true intentions.

rows.jp: 「鼻が……毎日洗濯ばさみで高くしているわらひの鼻がぁ……」
rows.en: “By dose... by poor dose I stretch with clothespins every day...”

ghs.en: Touko: "My nose... my pDecious nose Dat I Daise wif a cloDespin eBery day...!"

rows.jp: そんなことしてましたか。

ghs.en: So she has been doing that as well?

rows.en: “Are you seriously going to live here?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You really want to stay here?"

rows.jp: 「住むわよ！　もう決めたの！」

ghs.en: Touko: "I will be staying here! It's already decided!"
Taichi: "And you don't even show any shyness..."

rows.jp: 「おまえは、人のことをポンポン殴る勝ち気娘なんだけど鑑賞面においては俺に妙に都合の良い追従的なヒロインであれよっ！！」
rows.en: “You’re supposed to be the feisty heroine who slugs everybody—yet somehow turns conveniently submissive to me whenever it’s good for the audience!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You, you're always that unyielding spirit that punches people left and right, but in terms of artistic appreciation you're a heroine that finds an oddly convenient subservience in me!!!"
ghs.assessment: The narrator demands that although she is a strong-willed girl who hits people, for viewing purposes she should be a heroine conveniently compliant with him. 'Finds ... subservience in me' reverses who is compliant with whom and is not coherent English.
ghs.remedy: Use 'You may be a headstrong girl who hits people at every turn, but for my viewing pleasure, be a heroine conveniently submissive to me!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "You, you're always that unyielding spirit that punches people left and right, but in terms of artistic appreciation you're a heroine that finds an oddly convenient subservience in me!!!"

rows.en: “...I have no idea what you mean.”

ghs.en: Touko: "...I don't get what you're saying, no."
ghs.assessment: The source simply says she does not understand what he means. The final 'no' invents a verbal tag not characteristic of the line.
ghs.remedy: Use '...I don't understand what you're saying.'

highlights.text: Touko: "...I don't get what you're saying, no."

rows.jp: ふぁさぁっと後ろ髪をはらった。
rows.en: She swept back her hair with a fwoosh.

ghs.en: With a 'fwasah' I sweeped my bangs.
ghs.assessment: 後ろ髪 is the hair at the back of her head, not the narrator's bangs. 'Sweeped' is also not the past tense of 'sweep.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'With a soft swish, she brushes back her hair.'

highlights.text: With a 'fwasah' I sweeped my bangs.

rows.jp: 「さっきまで殊勝だったのに！」
rows.en: “You were acting so meek a minute ago!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "When you were so very admirable until moments ago!"
ghs.assessment: 殊勝 genuinely permits admirable or commendable, though context makes meek or contrite more pointed.
ghs.remedy: Use a context-sensitive contrition term.

highlights.text: Taichi: "When you were so very admirable until moments ago!"

rows.jp: 「言質を取ったらもうしおらしくする必要なんてないでしょ」
rows.en: “Now that I have your word, I don’t have to act meek anymore.”

ghs.en: Touko: "Once I got your commitment, being all meek is not necessary anymore is it."
ghs.assessment: The source gives a coherent rhetorical question. 'Being all meek is not necessary anymore is it' needs normal clause order and punctuation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Now that I have your word, I don't need to act meek anymore, do I?'

highlights.text: Touko: "Once I got your commitment, being all meek is not necessary anymore is it."

rows.jp: 「あーっ、ああああーっ、たばかったなーっ！」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ahhh, AAAAAH, I was taken iiin!"

rows.jp: 「警察がいないなら刀も堂々と持ってこられるわね」
rows.en: “With no police around, I can bring my sword over in broad daylight.”

ghs.en: Touko: "Since there's no police anymore, I can carry my sword openly now."

rows.jp: あの妖刀ハラキリ丸を我が家に！？
rows.en: That demon blade Harakiri-maru—in my house?!

ghs.en: The Demon Blade Harakiri, in my house!?
ghs.assessment: The weapon name is 妖刀ハラキリ丸, the demonic sword Harakiri-maru. 'Demon Blade Harakiri' omits the name-forming suffix -maru.
ghs.remedy: Use 'That demonic sword Harakiri-maru—in my house?!'

highlights.text: The Demon Blade Harakiri, in my house!?

rows.jp: 「ヒィィィィィィィッ、誰かーっ！　ここに刃物をすごく上手に使いこなす武士っ娘がいますっ！！」
rows.en: “HEEEEEELP! There’s a samurai girl here who really knows her way around a blade!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "HYYYYYYH! SOMEBODYYY! There's a samurai girl with great skill in the handling of cutting implements heeeere!!!"

rows.jp: 「誰か、なんてもういないでしょ」
rows.en: “There’s no one left to help you.”

ghs.assessment: そうでした is the narrator's immediate realization, 'That's right!' 'Indeed there wasn't' recasts it as a formal past-tense confirmation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'That's right!'

highlights.text: Indeed there wasn't!

rows.jp: 「だいたい、よく考えたらこれは正当な権利じゃない」
rows.en: “Come to think of it, I have every right to move in.”

ghs.en: Touko: "Besides, thinking hard about it, this is no unwarranted privilege."
ghs.assessment: よく考えたら means 'when I think about it,' not that she thinks hard. 正当な権利 is a legitimate right; 'no unwarranted privilege' substitutes a double-negative legal category.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Besides, now that I think about it, this is my legitimate right.'

highlights.text: Touko: "Besides, thinking hard about it, this is no unwarranted privilege."

rows.jp: 「駄目だっていうなら、返してよ」
rows.en: “If you’re going to say no, give it back.”

ghs.en: Touko: "If you say I cannot, then give it back."

rows.jp: 片手を突きつけられる。
rows.en: One hand shot out at me.

ghs.en: One hand was thrust before me.

rows.jp: 「『隣に住むＨな妹１８歳』ならもう返却済みだ……」
rows.en: “I already returned My Horny Eighteen-Year-Old Little Sister Next Door...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I've already returned 'My Neighbor Is An 18 Years Old Ecchi Imouto'..."
ghs.assessment: The mock title describes an eighteen-year-old sexy younger sister living next door. 'An 18 Years Old Ecchi Imouto' has incorrect age-compound grammar and leaves both descriptive nouns untranslated.
ghs.remedy: Use a grammatical English mock title such as 'My Sexy Eighteen-Year-Old Little Sister Next Door.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "I've already returned 'My Neighbor Is An 18 Years Old Ecchi Imouto'..."

rows.jp: 「エロビデオなんて貸してない！」

ghs.en: Touko: "I didn't lend you a porn video!"

rows.jp: 「もっと大切なものよ。ほら、返して」
rows.en: “Something more important. Come on, give it back.”

ghs.en: Touko: "This is something more precious. Come on, give it back."

rows.jp: 「『すこぶるスクブルすくぅる』も返却したはずだ……」
rows.en: “I’m sure I returned Super-Squirmy Schoolgirls too...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I think I have returned 'Blooming Boardschool Bloomers'..."

rows.jp: 「マニアビデオも貸してないっ！！」
rows.en: “I never lent you a fetish video either!”

ghs.en: Touko: "I didn't lend you a fetish video either!!!"

rows.jp: 「私の大切なもの！　あなたが奪ったでしょ！」
rows.en: “Something precious! You took it from me!”

ghs.en: Touko: "My most precious thing! The one you took from me by force!"

ghs.assessment: The source is the narrator's complete action of nodding broadly. 'A very big nod' is a subjectless noun phrase.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I nod broadly.'

highlights.text: A very big nod.

ghs.assessment: The Japanese speaker metadata identifies Tōko as the person demanding whether he has dementia. The English labels the line as Taichi, assigning the insult to its target.
ghs.remedy: Attribute the line to Tōko.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Have you got dementia, you?!"

rows.jp: 「とにかく住むの！　住みまくるの！　住みこんで住みあげて……住みぬくの！　もう決定！　可決！」
rows.en: “I’m moving in! I’m moving all the way in! Moving in, moving up, moving through—I’m moving in for good! Decision made! Motion carried!”

ghs.en: Touko: "Anyway, I'll be staying! Recklessly staying! Diving into staying to granting you my staying... thoroughly staying! Already decided! Ratified!"

rows.jp: 「半分で過半数ってことかーっ！？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "How did you get a majority when you're only haaalf?!"

rows.jp: 「すぐに荷物持ってきてやるんだから！」
rows.en: “I’m going to get my things right now!”

ghs.en: Touko: "So I'll be bringing over my luggage right quick!"
ghs.assessment: The source says she will bring her luggage immediately. 'So' adds a logical connector and 'right quick' adds marked dialect.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I'll bring my luggage over right away!'

highlights.text: Touko: "So I'll be bringing over my luggage right quick!"

ghs.en: She spins back on a heel.
ghs.assessment: きびすを返す is the idiom 'turn on one's heel.' 'Spins back on a heel' combines a different action and the wrong preposition.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She turns on her heel.'

highlights.text: She spins back on a heel.

ghs.assessment: やむを得ないか is a resigned conclusion that it cannot be helped. 'Is this unavoidable?' leaves the decision as an open information question.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I suppose it can't be helped.'

highlights.text: Is this unavoidable?

rows.jp: 「……なんとか……その線で納得してもらって……うん、よし」
rows.en: “...Somehow... I’ll get her to agree to that... Yeah. Okay.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...it's just... getting consent with that line... yes, got it."
ghs.assessment: The narrator mutters about somehow getting her to accept that line of reasoning. 'Getting consent with that line' changes persuasion into formal consent and leaves the clause without a subject.
ghs.remedy: Use '...Somehow get her to accept that reasoning... Yeah, good.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "...it's just... getting consent with that line... yes, got it."

rows.en: “Okay. I hereby approve your entry into the country.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Okieh, I will recognize your immigration."
ghs.assessment: The mock-border metaphor grants her entry into the narrator's territory. 'Recognize your immigration' describes official acknowledgment of a migration process, not permission to enter.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Okay. I hereby grant you entry.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Okieh, I will recognize your immigration."

rows.jp: 「ただし今日ってこたないだろ。明日でいいじゃないか」

ghs.en: Taichi: "However, today's a bit of a problem. Isn't it better tomorrow?"

rows.jp: 「部屋の掃除だってしないとならんし」
rows.en: “I need to clean the place first.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I gotta clean out the room at least, after all."
ghs.assessment: The source adds that the room also needs cleaning. 'At least' invents a minimum contrast.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I have to clean the room too.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "I gotta clean out the room at least, after all."

rows.jp: 「明日だったら、俺も荷物運ぶの手伝ってやるから」
rows.en: “Come tomorrow, and I’ll help carry your stuff.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "If we do this tomorrow, I can help you carry over the bags."
ghs.assessment: 荷物 is luggage or belongings in this moving context. 'Bags' narrows it to containers and can imply only hand baggage.
ghs.remedy: Use 'If it is tomorrow, I'll help you carry your things.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "If we do this tomorrow, I can help you carry over the bags."

rows.jp: ぱっと点灯する冬子スマイル。
rows.en: The Touko Smile lit up at once.

ghs.en: Touko smiles with the suddenness of a light bulb turned on.

ghs.assessment: 俺の芸術 is simply 'my art' in the narrator's trailing thought. 'My poor work of art' adds pity and turns the abstraction into a countable artwork.
ghs.remedy: Use 'My art...'

highlights.text: My poor work of art...

rows.jp: 「どっちにしても、すぐ帰って用意しないと」
rows.en: “Either way, I need to hurry home and get ready.”

ghs.en: Touko: "Regardless, I must go home and prepare things."

ghs.assessment: んだね is an agreeing 'Yeah' or 'Right.' 'So you do' makes the addressee's action the focus of a newly discovered proposition.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Yeah.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "So you do."

rows.jp: 「じゃあ明日ね。普通に学校に行くから」
rows.en: “See you tomorrow. I’ll come to school like normal.”

ghs.en: Touko: "See you tomorrow then. Since I'll be going to school as normal."
ghs.assessment: The speaker gives two sequential statements: see you tomorrow, and she will come to school normally. 'Since' falsely makes attending school the reason for the farewell.
ghs.remedy: Use 'See you tomorrow. I'll come to school as usual.'

highlights.text: Touko: "See you tomorrow then. Since I'll be going to school as normal."

rows.jp: 小さくなっていく冬子。
rows.en: Touko grew smaller in the distance.

ghs.en: Touko grows smaller and smaller as she goes.

rows.jp: 俺はいつまでもゆるゆると手を振っていた。
rows.en: I kept waving lazily until she disappeared from view.

ghs.en: I kept constantly, loosely, slowly waving a hand.
ghs.assessment: The source says he kept waving languidly for a long time. 'Kept constantly, loosely, slowly' stacks incompatible adverbs and redundantly expresses duration.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I kept waving lazily for a long time.'

highlights.text: I kept constantly, loosely, slowly waving a hand.

rows.jp: 厄介なことになったなぁ……。
rows.en: Well, this was going to be a pain...

ghs.en: This has become awkward, didn't it...
ghs.assessment: Awkward can mean troublesome or difficult. The confirmed defect is the malformed tag tense.
ghs.remedy: Repair the tag question.

highlights.text: This has become awkward, didn't it...
